reviewer: Claude Code agent executing C06 (each prompt/target pair read in full)
sampling_note: Repaired rows: stratified by source variant x finish kind (source_ref in the context sidecar), fixed floor of 5 for the five small strata and a proportional split of the rest; within a stratum, random.Random(3407).sample over sorted row ids, strata in sorted order. Controls: a fresh random.Random(3407).sample of 20 over the sorted ids of the 4,282 unrepaired finish_block rows.

class_definitions.correct: The applied document parses; the target completes exactly the block(s) the prompt leaves open, ending with the closing brace and nothing after it; any old region text is re-emitted; the code is consistent with the file's own style and plausibly the source's continuation.
class_definitions.cosmetic: Correct code that parses and is semantically right, but has a style inconsistency with the surrounding file (here: the closing brace is indented differently from the line that opens its block).
class_definitions.defective: Does not parse, leaves a block open or closes too much, swallows or duplicates post-cursor code, drops typed text, or is semantically wrong or incomplete relative to the prompt (the postmortem's 'semantic drift / incomplete setup').

caveats: One reviewer and no second rater. Semantic correctness was judged by reading, not by running the code.

The data's build receipts record no air version. Checks used air 0.12.0. air rewrapped lines inside 36 of 80 repaired and 8 of 20 control targets. All of these follow the file's own pre-air style (rewrapping, braces around one-line ifs), so they are not counted as issues. air was idempotent and error-free on all 100 rows.

No finish_block row has post-cursor text: suffix_lines is empty and the replacement range ends at EOF for all 7,785 rows. 'Swallowing post-cursor code' was therefore checked as 'nothing after the closing brace, and the closing brace matches a block the prompt opened'. Nothing was swallowed.

The cosmetic brace-indent pattern is systematic. The census found it in 486 of 3,503 repaired rows (13.9%), all in compound* strata, and in 0 of 4,282 unrepaired rows. In every sampled case but one, the body keeps 2 more spaces of indentation than the closing brace while the header sits at column 0. Combined with free variables from an enclosing scope, this points to nested function definitions lifted with only the header dedented. The fix appends the source brace byte-exact, so the brace keeps the original nested indentation.
